hook.situation: A friend asks, '어제 뭐 했어요?' If you answer in present tense — 영화 봐요, 밥 먹어요 — it sounds like you are talking about your usual routine or what you do now. For yesterday, Korean needs the polite past frame: 봤어요, 먹었어요, 갔어요, 했어요.
objectives: Choose 았어요 vs 었어요 from the last vowel of the stem
Handle the first everyday contractions and irregulars: 했어요, 봤어요, 왔어요, 추웠어요
hook.whyItMatters: Past tense is the grammar that lets beginners tell real stories. You use it after class, on KakaoTalk, when explaining why you are late, and any time someone asks what happened. A clean short past sentence sounds much more natural than a long sentence with the wrong tense.

grammarNotes.title: V았/었어요 — Polite Past Tense
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Think of -았/었어요 as a PAST SNAPSHOT. The event is finished, and you are showing one photo from yesterday, last week, or earlier today. The ending carries the time: 먹어요 is now/usual; 먹었어요 is a finished snapshot.
grammarNotes.formation: 1) Remove 다 from the dictionary form. 2) If the last vowel of the stem is ㅏ or ㅗ, add -았어요. 3) For most other vowels, add -었어요. 4) 하다 becomes 했어요. Common contractions: 가다→갔어요, 오다→왔어요, 보다→봤어요. First irregular to learn: ㅂ irregular adjectives such as 춥다 become 추웠어요.

examples.note: 먹다 stem 먹- has ㅓ/ㅏ? The vowel is ㅓ-side for this rule, so use -었어요: 먹었어요.

examples.en: I watched a movie with a friend.
examples.note: 보다 + 았어요 contracts to 봤어요. This is one of the most useful past forms.

examples.en: I went to Korea last year.

examples.note: 하다 becomes 했어요, not 하었어요. This question is the chapter's anchor.

examples.en: The weather was cold, but it was fun.
examples.note: 춥다 is ㅂ irregular: 춥- drops ㅂ and becomes 추웠어요. 재미있다 takes -었어요: 재미있었어요.

a.en: I watch movies / I am watching a movie.

contrastPairs.explanation: 봐요 can describe a current or habitual action. 봤어요 marks a completed past event.

b.en: I was meeting / was with a friend.

contrastPairs.explanation: -았/었어요 gives the finished event. -고 있었어요 describes what was in progress at that past moment.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English learners often keep the familiar present form and rely on 'yesterday' to do the time work. Korean still expects the verb ending to match the time. 어제 plus 봐요 clashes; use 봤어요.

exceptions: 하다 → 했어요 is a must-memorize shortcut: 공부했어요, 일했어요, 전화했어요.
오다 and 보다 contract: 왔어요, 봤어요. Saying 오았어요 or 보았어요 sounds written or unnatural in everyday speech.
ㅂ irregular adjectives such as 춥다 and 덥다 become 추웠어요, 더웠어요. Do not say 춥었어요.

exampleSentence.note: 어제 almost always pulls the sentence into past tense.

exampleSentence.en: I went to Busan last week.
exampleSentence.note: 지난주에 marks when the completed event happened.

exampleSentence.en: I came to Korea last year.
exampleSentence.note: 오다 becomes 왔어요 in the past.

exampleSentence.en: I ate dinner at a restaurant.
I watched a movie with a friend.
I went to Busan last week.
I went to a cafe with a friend.
exampleSentence.note: 친구랑 is natural in casual polite conversation.

exampleSentence.en: The movie was a little long.
exampleSentence.note: Adjectives also take past tense: 길다 → 길었어요.
Use 에서 for where the action happened.

readingText.title: 어제 한 일
readingText.body: 어제는 수업이 끝난 뒤에 친구를 만났어요. 같이 카페에 갔고, 저는 커피를 마셨어요. 친구는 차를 마셨어요. 그다음 영화를 봤어요. 영화는 조금 길었지만 마지막 장면이 정말 재미있었어요. 집에 올 때는 날씨가 추웠어요. 그래서 집에 오자마자 따뜻한 물을 마시고 바로 잤어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Yesterday, after class ended, I met a friend. We went to a cafe together, and I drank coffee. My friend drank tea. Then we watched a movie. The movie was a little long, but the last scene was really fun. When I came home, the weather was cold. So as soon as I got home, I drank warm water and went straight to sleep.

comprehensionQuestions.question: What did the writer do after class?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 친구를 만났어요 and 같이 카페에 갔어요.

culturalNote.title: Short Past Answers Sound Natural
culturalNote.body: When Koreans ask 어제 뭐 했어요?, they are often opening a small everyday conversation, not asking for a long report. A natural answer can be short: 친구 만났어요, 영화 봤어요, 집에서 쉬었어요. Once the tense is clean, you can add one detail: 누구랑, 어디에서, 어땠는지. Accurate short past sentences are better than long translated sentences with the wrong ending.
culturalNote.tip: Answer in one finished event first, then add time, person, or place.
